theme: Late-summer seafood, built on a jar of confit tomatoes and a quick fumet — a 2-adult, technique-forward week

components.name: Confit cherry tomatoes (olive-oil conserva)
components.ingredients: 2 lb cherry/Sungold tomatoes, 6 garlic cloves, thyme + a strip of orange peel, chili flake, ~1.5 cups olive oil, flaky salt
components.method: Heat oven to 300°F. Nestle whole tomatoes, smashed garlic, thyme and orange peel in a small baking dish and pour olive oil until they're half-submerged. Salt lightly. Bake 60–75 min until slumped and jammy but not broken down. Cool and store submerged in their oil; they keep 1–2 weeks fridge and turn any pan into dinner.

components.name: Quick fish fumet
components.ingredients: 1.5 lb white-fish bones/heads (or shrimp shells), 1 leek, 1 fennel stalk, 1 celery rib, 1 cup dry white wine, parsley stems, bay
components.method: Rinse bones well to keep the stock clean. Sweat the sliced aromatics in olive oil with no color, 6–8 min. Add bones, wine, cover with cold water. Bring just to a bare simmer, skim the gray foam, and hold 20 min — no longer or it turns bitter. Strain, cool, chill. Freeze half in a jar for later weeks.

dinners.name: Crisp-skin branzino with confit tomatoes & basil
dinners.ingredients: 2 branzino fillets (or sea bass), confit tomatoes + a spoon of their oil, basil, lemon
steps: Pat fillets bone-dry; salt the skin. Lay skin-down in a cold nonstick pan, then bring heat to medium-high.
Press gently 30 sec so it stays flat; cook 3–4 min until skin is crackling and the flesh has gone opaque up the sides.
Flip for just 30–45 sec, then rest skin-up.
Warm a few confit tomatoes in their oil, spoon around the fish, finish with basil and lemon.

dinners.name: Seafood brodetto on the fumet
dinners.ingredients: fumet, confit tomatoes, mixed fish + shrimp, clams or mussels, garlic, grilled bread
steps: Bloom garlic and chili in olive oil, add a few confit tomatoes and crush lightly.
Add the fumet and a splash of wine; simmer 10 min to a light broth.
Slide in firm fish first, then shrimp and shellfish; cover until the shells open and fish is just set.
Ladle over garlic-rubbed grilled bread, big drizzle of raw olive oil.

dinners.name: Spaghetti al pomodoro confit with anchovy
dinners.ingredients: spaghetti, confit tomatoes + oil, 3 anchovies, garlic, parmigiano or toasted breadcrumbs
steps: Melt anchovies and garlic in the confit oil until dissolved.
Add a ladle of pasta water and the confit tomatoes; smash into a loose sauce.
Toss just-shy-of-done spaghetti in the pan and mantecare with more pasta water until glossy.
Finish with cheese or crunchy breadcrumbs.

dinners.name: Clams in fumet-tomato broth with fennel
dinners.ingredients: littleneck clams, fumet, confit tomatoes, shaved fennel, white wine, parsley
steps: Sweat shaved fennel in olive oil until soft.
Add wine and reduce, then fumet and a spoon of confit tomatoes.
Add clams, cover, and steam 4–6 min until they open; discard any that stay shut.
Shower with parsley and serve with more grilled bread for the broth.

technique.name: Cold-pan crisp fish skin
technique.tiedTo: The branzino — starting skin-down in a cold pan and coming up to heat renders the skin evenly so it shatters instead of curling; the same trick carries every seared-fish dinner all week.

shopping.items: 2 lb cherry/Sungold tomatoes, 2 heads garlic, 1 leek, 1 fennel bulb (+stalk), 1 celery rib, basil, parsley, thyme, 1 orange, 2 lemons
2 branzino fillets, ~1.5 lb white-fish bones or shrimp shells, mixed fish for brodetto, shrimp, littleneck clams, mussels
good olive oil (large bottle), anchovies, spaghetti, dry white wine, chili flake, bay, flaky salt, rustic bread for grilling

scaleNote: This is a 2-adult, technique week (girls with Jen through Aug 23). For a full-house week later, double the confit tomatoes and make a full 750ml fumet; anchor the kids on the spaghetti al pomodoro (pull anchovies for the wary) and serve the branzino as simply pan-seared fillets. For 6, plan ~2 branzino fillets per 2 kids sharing, 3 lb clams, and 1.25 lb spaghetti.
